header.title: Panarion (Adversus Haereses): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Epiphanius
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg2021.tlg002.1st1K-grc1, from Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg2021.tlg002.1st1K-gr: The text repeats words ('ἅμα ἅμα γόητες γόητες'), a dittography. 'τινας' seems to lack its noun, or goes with 'incantations' (ἐπιορκισμούς).
'ὑπερ- άνω' is read as ὑπεράνω. 'Ἀβασάξ' is a slip for Abrasax. The 'numerical value' (ψῆφος) is the sum of the letters taken as numbers.

nodes.text: And he says that the power and principle above these is Abrasax, because the numerical value of Abrasax holds the number three hundred and sixty-five, so that from this he tries to establish the evidence for his myth-making about the three hundred and sixty-five heavens.

Some say that Sabaoth has the form of an ass, others of a pig; and for this reason, he says, he commanded the Jews not to eat pig. And [they say] that he is the maker of heaven and earth, and of the heavens after him, and of his own angels.
There the sorcerers together took the aforementioned [young man] and worked upon him certain incantations and practices full of impiety, and in the name of the aforementioned woman.
